# Part I — Getting started

How fuel injection works, the pieces of a rusEFI system, the two programs you will use, and the path from a new ECU to a first connection and a first start. Start here if rusEFI is new to you.

- **[How EFI works](how-efi-works.md)** — An electronic fuel injection (EFI) computer measures how much air the engine is taking in and where the crankshaft is, works out how much fuel to spray and when to fire the spark, and switches the injectors and coils at exactly the right crank angle — hundreds of times a second.
- **[The rusEFI system](rusefi-system.md)** — A rusEFI installation is an ECU board running a firmware build made for that board, a bootloader that lets you replace that firmware, and two programs on your PC — TunerStudio and the rusEFI console — that both come with a matching set of files called a bundle.
- **[Your two tools](two-tools.md)** — If you're changing how the engine runs, use TunerStudio; if you're looking after the ECU itself, use the rusEFI console.
- **[Installing the software](installing.md)** — You install TunerStudio MS to set up and tune the engine, MegaLogViewer HD to read logs, and the rusEFI bundle for your board — the rusEFI console, firmware and drivers in one folder — to look after the ECU itself.
- **[Flashing firmware](flashing-firmware.md)** — Flashing writes a new rusEFI firmware into the ECU's processor — normally with one button in the rusEFI console, which saves your tune first and puts it back afterwards — and it leaves your settings where they are.
- **[First connection](first-connection.md)** — You plug the ECU into your computer with a USB cable, create a TunerStudio project that uses the `.ini` file from your firmware bundle, go online, and learn to read the front page before you change anything.
- **[Quick start](quick-start.md)** — The fifteen steps from an ECU in its box to a running, logged engine, in the order to do them, with the TunerStudio dialog for each and the chapter that explains it.
